quick: 500-1000 mg up to 4 times daily (max ~4 g/day)
Take with water; with food if GI upset
CBC - stop and check if fever/sore throat (agranulocytosis)
summary: Metamizole (dipyrone) is a pyrazolone non-opioid analgesic, antipyretic and spasmolytic used for severe pain (including colic) and refractory high fever in many countries. It is NOT approved in the United States and was withdrawn from several markets because of the risk of agranulocytosis. Usual adult dose is 500-1000 mg up to four times daily. The defining safety concern is potentially fatal agranulocytosis; patients must stop the drug and have a blood count if fever, chills, sore throat or mouth ulcers develop.
indications: Severe acute or chronic pain not responding to other measures
Pain associated with smooth-muscle spasm (renal, biliary or intestinal colic)
High fever unresponsive to other antipyretics

dosage.n: Maximum about 4 g/day; use shortest effective course

dosage.d: 1000-2500 mg per dose (slow IV); max ~5 g/day in some SmPCs
dosage.n: Slow IV to avoid hypotension; monitor BP

dosage.d: 8-16 mg/kg per dose (per SmPC, age/weight restrictions apply)

admin: Take oral doses with a glass of water; with food if it upsets the stomach
Give intravenous doses slowly (over several minutes) with the patient lying down and blood pressure monitored to avoid hypotension/shock
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time
Stop immediately and check a blood count if signs of agranulocytosis appear
moa: Metamizole is a prodrug; after hydrolysis its active metabolites (notably 4-methylaminoantipyrine) inhibit cyclooxygenase and reduce prostaglandin synthesis centrally and peripherally, producing analgesia and antipyresis. It also has a spasmolytic (smooth-muscle relaxant) action useful in colicky pain, and possible central and cannabinoid-related analgesic mechanisms.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to metamizole, other pyrazolones or pyrazolidines
History of agranulocytosis or other blood dyscrasia from any drug

preg: Avoid in pregnancy. Use is contraindicated in the third trimester because of the risk of premature closure of the ductus arteriosus and effects on the fetus/labor, and it should be avoided in the first trimester; data in the second trimester are limited.
lact: Avoid breastfeeding around the time of use - metabolites of metamizole are excreted into breast milk; if a single dose is unavoidable, breastfeeding should be withheld for about 48 hours.
renal: Use with caution and avoid high or prolonged doses in renal impairment; metabolites are renally eliminated and can accumulate. Avoid in severe renal failure.
hepatic: Use with caution and reduce exposure in hepatic impairment; avoid high doses and avoid in severe hepatic failure.

major: Other agents causing agranulocytosis/myelosuppression (e.g., methotrexate) - additive hematologic toxicity
Ciclosporin - metamizole may lower ciclosporin levels
moderate: Other NSAIDs - additive GI and renal effects
Antihypertensives/diuretics - blunted effect and hypotension risk
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce gastric upset; no major food interaction.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol because of additive central and hepatic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause red discoloration of urine (rubazonic acid); may lower neutrophil/white cell counts.

monitoring: Complete blood count, especially if therapy is prolonged or signs of infection appear
Immediate CBC and discontinuation if fever, chills, sore throat or mouth ulcers occur
counsel: Stop the medicine at once and get a blood test if you develop fever, chills, sore throat or mouth ulcers
Your urine may turn reddish - this is harmless
Use only at the lowest dose and for the shortest time needed
Avoid alcohol and do not take other painkillers without advice
Tell your doctor about any past reaction to painkillers or any blood disorder
pk: Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved and withdrawn in several countries (USA, UK, others) due to risk of fatal agranulocytosis - data here are based on EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
Hallmark danger is agranulocytosis: educate patients to stop and seek a blood count for fever/sore throat
Give intravenous doses slowly with the patient supine to prevent hypotension/shock
Contraindicated in pyrazolone allergy, G6PD deficiency, acute porphyria and bone marrow disorders
missed: Metamizole is generally used as needed for pain or fever rather than on a fixed schedule. If on a scheduled regimen, take a missed dose when remembered unless the next dose is near, then skip it - do not double up, and do not exceed the daily maximum.
overdose: Overdose can cause nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, hypotension, tachycardia, drowsiness, seizures, red urine, and hepatic/renal injury; severe cases may cause coma and bone marrow toxicity. There is no specific antidote - give supportive care, activated charcoal if early, forced diuresis or hemodialysis for the dialyzable metabolites, and monitor blood counts and organ function.
